extracted.intended_audience: individual humanities scholars applying for NEH Summer Stipends (2019)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting an application to the National Endowment for the Humanities Summer Stipends program, including eligibility, formatting, reference letters, submission via Grants.gov, and review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project significance and applicant qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants must propose a significant project and must also present evidence of their qualifications, including publications, presentations, and other relevant experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will assess the project’s significance and the applicant’s demonstrated qualifications via submitted records (publications, presentations, relevant experience). See Program Statistics on the program resource page for funding ratio information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate student degree conferral requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduate students are not eligible unless they have satisfied all degree requirements and are awaiting conferral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants awaiting conferral must include a letter from the dean of the conferring school attesting to the applicant’s status as of September 25, 2019; that letter must be included as an appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application narrative format limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative may not exceed three single-spaced pages, and the font should not be smaller than 11 point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must follow the format given in the Notice of Funding Opportunity. Applications that violate the format instructions will not be reviewed or will be declared ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices: eligibility and length limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices may be added only for specified project types and for certain special circumstances; appendices may not exceed one single-spaced page per item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed appendices include those for editions, translations, database projects, projects that include visual materials, applicants awaiting degree conferral, or applicants with federal debt. Other appendices are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline strictness and late submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No deadline extensions are possible; late applications will be declared ineligible and will not be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure timely submission and receipt/validation by Grants.gov and NEH before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of project and dissemination explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects whose results will be written in a language other than English are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants whose work will be written in another language must explain how access and dissemination will be affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation proposals when other English translations exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may apply to translate a work into English even if other English translations already exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal narrative must provide a rationale for producing a new translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual award requirement and collaborative-project guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Summer Stipends program is designed for individual researchers; awards may not be divided among collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If funding is sought for more than one participant in a collaborative project, each person must submit a separate application specifying their individual contribution. Each application should clearly explain how the work will be divided and how dependent each contributor’s work is on others. Applicants working as part of a collaborative team but seeking funding only for themselves are eligible. Consider applying for an NEH Collaborative Research award if proposing to work together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of award period for revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a Summer Stipend to revise work is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work plans must not depend entirely upon factors outside an applicant’s control; for example, Summer Stipends should not be used to respond to pending or anticipated readers’ reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative NEH and partner fellowship opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH offers other fellowship programs for individual scholars for different durations and eligibility rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH Fellowships, NEH-Mellon, Public Scholar, and Awards for Faculty have differing durations and eligibility (e.g., Awards for Faculty limited to certain institutions). NEH also collaborates with other institutions (LOC, JUSFC, DEL program) — applicants should consult those programs directly when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding one NEH individual award at a time
rubrics_metrics.description: You may hold only one NEH award for individuals at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When awards are held in close sequence you may need to delay the start of the second award to avoid overlap. If you accept a Fellowship in the same fiscal year in which you apply for a Summer Stipend, the Summer Stipends application will be automatically withdrawn after you accept the Fellowship; contact program staff for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help available and staff limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH staff cannot comment on draft proposals because of volume, but will answer questions about preparing your proposal and about eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to review samples of previously funded applications (linked on the program resource page). Contact staff at (202) 606-8200 or stipends@neh.gov for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting disciplinary fields for interdisciplinary projects
rubrics_metrics.description: On the NEH Supplemental Information for Individuals Form you may select up to three disciplinary fields that characterize your project; list the primary field first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you select more than one, list the primary field first. In selecting referees, choose two who can effectively attest to your ability to work in the relevant disciplines. Program staff will use this information to assign your application to an appropriate review panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project title requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Your title should be brief (not exceeding 125 characters) and descriptive of the project, free of specialized language that might not be understood by the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid a main title that requires clarification by the subtitle. When possible include places and dates indicating scope. If a person is mentioned, include dates and description. Use informative and specific words rather than puzzling or intriguing phrasing. Omit technical terms, jargon, and unfamiliar words. NEH reserves the right to re-title funded projects that do not follow agency guidelines, though award recipients may use their preferred title for award products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination requirement for tenured and tenure-track faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: All tenured and tenure-track faculty must be nominated by their institution; each institution can nominate up to two people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-tenure-track faculty, staff, and independent scholars are exempt from this requirement. The nomination requirement is designed to invite applications from a wide variety of institutions and to encourage on-campus discussion about research and peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referees: submission methods and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH strongly encourages referees to submit letters online; if not possible, referees may e-mail letters to stipends@neh.gov or fax them to 202-606-8204.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH will contact referees approximately seven to ten days after the application deadline. You will be notified by e-mail when each letter has been received. After receiving the Grants.gov Agency Tracking Number Assignment message, you may check status by logging into NEH’s secure site to see names and e-mail addresses of letter writers and whether letters have arrived. Do not contact referees about non-arrival until you know they’ve received requests from NEH. Incorrect or multiple e-mail addresses, or addresses referees do not check, will prevent NEH from sending requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing referees after the deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to change a referee after the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact program staff at stipends@neh.gov or 202-606-8200; indicate which referee to replace and provide contact information including e-mail for the new referee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late letters of reference policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Late letters of reference are accepted and will be added to your file when uploaded by the referee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if an external reviewer has already reviewed the file, it is unlikely that he or she will take the late letter into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing letters of reference policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A missing letter of reference does not disqualify an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications remain eligible for review and award, but evaluators may find the application less persuasive if one or both letters are missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review and decision process
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications receive peer review by scholars in the humanities, who read and rate applications using the review criteria listed in Section II of the application guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH staff comment on matters of fact or significant issues missing from reviews, then make recommendations to the National Council on the Humanities. The National Council advises the NEH chairman, who, by law, makes all funding decisions. Applicants may request reviewers’ comments after the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov submission, validation, and tracking responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission Grants.gov sends up to five e-mail messages at different stages (Submission Receipt; Validation Receipt or rejection with errors; Agency Retrieval Receipt when NEH uploads; Grants.gov Agency Tracking Number Assignment including NEH application number; and final Agency Notes indicating NEH acceptance or rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants.gov must validate the application prior to the deadline; if Grants.gov rejects for errors you must correct and resubmit (you will receive a new Grants.gov tracking number). NEH then checks that attachments are proper PDF format; if NEH rejects, you must correct and resubmit before the deadline. Grants.gov normally sends these messages within 24 hours but delays can occur. If you receive a rejection message, read it to determine what to fix. If you don’t receive all messages, check spam, use Grants.gov Track my Application, or contact Grants.gov (1-800-518-GRANTS or support@grants.gov). Include the Grants.gov tracking number in correspondence. It is your responsibility to confirm that Grants.gov and NEH have received and validated/accepted your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming and component limits for Grants.gov validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov validation can fail for specific errors such as exceeding character limits in a component or file name exceeding character limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If validation fails, Grants.gov rejects the application and sends a message explaining the error; correct the problem and resubmit before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory forms (Application for Federal Domestic Assistance – Individual Form)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Application for Federal Domestic Assistance – Individual Form is a required government form included in the 'Mandatory Documents' field of the application package in Grants.gov Workspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To begin filling out the form, click on the form in the Workspace. See Section III of the guidelines for discussion of Form I under STEP 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: DUNS number requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: DUNS stands for 'Data Universal Numbering System' and consists of nine digits; institutions have DUNS numbers issued by Dun & Bradstreet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have institutional affiliation you should obtain this number from your sponsored research office. More information about DUNS numbers is available via the provided link.
